tagline: Ops platform in a scalable portfolio monorepo
description: A session-authenticated ops dashboard I built into this site on purpose — finance, credentials, projects, resumes, and developer utilities in one codebase. The portfolio repo was designed to scale from day one, so a multi-tenant-capable product surface could grow here without a second stack or a performance rewrite. Demo mode keeps private ops data out of review sessions.

caseStudy.problem: Day-to-day ops work was scattered across separate budget, credentials, notes, finance, and utility tools — duplicate logins and no single source of truth. Spinning up a separate product repo would have duplicated auth, deploy, and scaling foundations.
caseStudy.constraints: Ship on the same Express/Vite portfolio server; keep owner vs demo (multi-tenant-style) data isolation; add modules over time without compromising structure or performance.
caseStudy.approach: From the start, structure the portfolio monorepo to scale — layered routes/services/repositories, modular /dashboard/* UI, shared session auth — then build Sree Dev Tool as a first-class product inside that foundation instead of a bolt-on demo.
results: One production dashboard replacing fragmented personal tools
Eight modular domains behind shared auth and tenant-style data isolation
Proof that the same scalable foundation can absorb new product features without a rewrite
reviewable: Application source in github.com/Sree0405/dev-portfolio (same scalable monorepo as this site)
Live demo login with sandboxed demo data — private ops records stay isolated
Architecture tab — system diagram, data flow, and How it ships
Security + Workflow tabs and per-module API notes
caseStudy.sourceNote: There is no separate Dev Tool repository by design. I made the portfolio repo scalable first so a multi-tenant-capable ops product could live here and keep growing modules without splitting stacks or compromising performance. Personal finance/credentials data stays private — demo mode and DataType isolation keep reviewer sessions on seeded data only.

overview.whyBuilt: I started the portfolio repo to be scalable from day one — layered server, modular UI, shared auth — so a full multi-tenant-capable Dev Tool could live in the same codebase later. At the same time I needed one ops surface: budget, credentials, notes, finance, and resume work were scattered across too many apps. Building Dev Tool into the portfolio proved the foundation: grow product features without a second stack or a rewrite.
overview.whatWeDo: Sree Dev Tool is a modular ops platform: projects and payments, credentials, budgets, EMI/subscriptions, LaTeX resumes, developer utilities, and a sandboxed playground — one login with owner/demo data isolation (tenant-style boundaries) so reviewers explore without seeing private records.
overview.howWeDo: Each capability is an independent module: Prisma models, repository → service → route layers on the backend, and dedicated React pages under /dashboard/*. Client-only modules (Playground) skip the API. A shared Express server serves both the Vite SPA and REST API, with Neon PostgreSQL via Prisma — the same process as the public portfolio.

architecture.sourcePolicy: Source is public in github.com/Sree0405/dev-portfolio — the same monorepo as this portfolio (server/, src/app/). The repo was built to scale from day one so a multi-tenant-capable Dev Tool could ship here and grow modules without a second codebase. Ops data stays private via owner/demo isolation; use demo login to explore without real records.
architecture.summary: Sree Dev Tool runs on the same Express server as the portfolio. In development, Vite middleware serves the React SPA; in production, Express serves the built dist/ folder. All API routes live under /api/* with session-based authentication.

frontendPattern: src/app/components/ → Shared UI (Modal, Table, Forms, Sidebar)
dataFlow: User logs in via POST /api/login — session stored in HTTP-only cookie
Frontend fetches data with credentials: include on all API calls
Repository layer filters all queries by session user's DataType
Business logic (totals, status, schedules) computed server-side only
Frontend renders with TanStack React Query for caching and refetching
deployment: Dev: single process — Express + Vite middleware on port 8080 (tsx watch)
Prod build: Vite outputs dist/; Express serves the SPA and /api/* from one Node process
Database: Neon PostgreSQL through Prisma migrations and seed for demo data
Auth/secrets: OWNER_* and SESSION_SECRET via environment — never committed
Review path: clone github.com/Sree0405/dev-portfolio; demo login for product feel; architecture/security tabs for the ship story

security.summary: Security is built around session authentication, strict data isolation between owner and demo accounts, server-side financial calculations, and masked credential display in the UI.
authentication: Session-based auth with HTTP-only cookies — no JWT or OAuth
Owner account configured via OWNER_USERNAME and OWNER_PASSWORD env vars
Demo account (username: Demo) for safe portfolio exploration
POST /api/logout destroys session; unauthenticated /dashboard/* redirects to /login
Session cookies are secure in production (NODE_ENV=production)
dataIsolation: Every data model includes a type field (DataType enum: Default | Demo)
Owner sees only Default data; Demo sees only Demo data
Demo users cannot delete records — UI hides delete buttons and API returns 403
Demo data seeded via prisma/seed.ts with fictional credentials and finance records
type field set automatically from session — never accepted from client
practices: Never commit .env or real credentials to the repository
All API routes validate input with Zod on the server
Passwords masked in UI by default — reveal requires explicit user action
Financial calculations never trusted from the client
15 MB body limit on resume save for PDF attachments

workflow.title: Login
workflow.description: User navigates to /login and authenticates with owner or demo credentials. Session cookie is set and user is redirected to /dashboard.

workflow.title: Dashboard Overview
workflow.description: Analytics home loads aggregated stats, charts, and recent activity in a single API call. User gets instant visibility into business health.

workflow.title: Module Navigation
workflow.description: User selects a module from the sidebar (Projects, Credentials, Finance, Resume, etc.). Each module loads its own page with scoped data.

workflow.title: CRUD Operations
workflow.description: User creates, views, edits, or deletes records within a module. Forms validate with Zod; mutations invalidate React Query caches.

workflow.title: Financial Actions
workflow.description: For projects: add payments with automatic total recalculation. For finance: mark payments as paid with append-only history. Download PDF reports.

workflow.title: Developer Tools
workflow.description: User opens Dev Utilities for quick encoding/formatting tasks, or Playground for sandboxed code execution — both without leaving the dashboard.

workflow.title: Logout
workflow.description: POST /api/logout destroys the session. User is redirected to /login. All dashboard routes become inaccessible.
